name: Mavi
label: Mavi 4 Mayor Music
lede: A Howard neuroscience student from Charlotte drops a debut, gets co-signed by Earl Sweatshirt, loses a whole album to sample clearance, then makes a 16-track record about grief that Pitchfork ranks No. 34 of 2022.

eras.title: Fourteen, and already a collective
eras.text: Omavi Minder starts rapping as a freshman in Charlotte and helps found the KILLSWITCH crew. Two mixtapes later he is still mostly a local secret.

years.src: Rolling Stone · The FADER · Wikipedia: Mavi
years.h: Rapping at 14, Mavi joins the KILLSWITCH collective
years.p: Omavi Minder, born in Sumter, South Carolina and raised in North Charlotte, starts rapping in his freshman year and comes up in the North Carolina crew KILLSWITCH.
years.xp:
Mavi has told The FADER that Charlotte felt stunting at first, with few peers who matched his lyrics and ear. KILLSWITCH was the fix: a rap collective of like-minded Charlotte artists that he co-founded.

Wikipedia dates his emergence with the group to 2014. His father was a hip-hop producer and gospel quartet singer, a lineage Mavi has pointed to in interviews as central to how he hears music.

years.p: Mavi's first solo release, put out from Charlotte while he was still a teenager.

years.h: No Roses and the first KILLSWITCH compilation
years.p: Mavi follows Beacon with the No Roses mixtape and appears on Rosewood Records Presents: Killswitch 2017 with the collective.

eras.title: Sun talk, and a famous co-sign
eras.text: A debut made at Howard University lands with Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE, two of rap's more selective ears, and a trip to Los Angeles follows.

years.cap: Cover of Let the Sun Talk (2019)
years.src: Wikipedia: Let the Sun Talk · DJBooth · The FADER
years.h: Let the Sun Talk: a Howard student's debut, 13 tracks, 32 minutes
years.p: Released independently while Mavi was at Howard University, it is built on Marvin Gaye's What's Going On and the writing of Toni Morrison.
years.xp:
The title draws on the Five-Percent Nation idea of the sun as knowledge and on Rastafari's "I and I." Mavi told DJBooth that letting the sun talk "is about getting in your 'I and I' bag." Producers include Tairiq, Duckie, Ntvrme, Dkarim, Murky Waters and Nephew Hesh, with Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE credited under aliases.

Sheldon Pearce of Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and wrote that it "lacks clarity and directness at times."

years.h: A verse on Earl Sweatshirt's Feet of Clay, then three or four days at Alchemist's
years.p: Mavi guests on [[Earl Sweatshirt|8b22acd6-20e6-4463-a75c-c14b5cfdb666]]'s EP, and Earl connects him with [[The Alchemist|03f3deb7-0419-4bf9-a1e7-511946385717]].
years.xp:
On that first LA trip in late 2019 Mavi spent "three or four days" in Alchemist's studio, Rolling Stone reported. Mavi recalled telling him, "Bro, I love to rap." Alchemist later said that unprompted line told him Mavi was "the one."

Mavi has described the stretch as being trained up: "He was training me up for real."

eras.title: The album that didn't come out
eras.text: Mavi announces a second album in a year of uprisings, then can't get it out. An EP and a collective tape fill the gap.

years.h: Shango gets a cover, a tracklist and sweatshirts, but no release
years.p: Sample clearance and other snags stop Mavi's announced second album.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reports Shango was made in the months after the George Floyd and Breonna Taylor protests and reached its final stage, with the cover, tracklist and merchandise done. Sample clearance and other problems kept it off the shelves.

The unsold black Shango sweatshirts are still boxed in his studio. Mavi has called Laughing So Hard, It Hurts a sister album to it.

years.p: The short project that keeps Mavi's name moving while Shango sits in the vault. The same year the KILLSWITCH crew returns with Rosewood Records Presents: Killswitch Vol. 2.

eras.title: Laughing so hard, it hurts
eras.text: A record about losing family, made in Charlotte, is the one that finally lands everywhere.

years.h: He writes nearly every song in January and adds two weeks before delivery
years.p: "I wrote almost all the songs in January, and I added two more like literally weeks before the album was turned in," Mavi told Passion of the Weiss.
years.xp: He recorded in Charlotte, and by his account wrote around ten tracks without drums, leaving room for melody and his voice. He also said attempts to land features from Earl Sweatshirt and Noname did not work out, so he made the record alone: "It's meant for me to do the marathon."

years.cap: Cover of Laughing So Hard, It Hurts (2022)
years.src: Album of the Year · BrooklynVegan · Rolling Stone
years.h: Laughing So Hard, It Hurts: 16 tracks, self-released, Pitchfork 8.2
years.p: Pitchfork gave Paul A. Thompson's review 8.2 and ranked the album No. 34 of 2022.
years.xp:
Mavi put the album out himself on Mavi 4 Mayor Music. Lead single "Baking Soda" was produced by Monte Booker, and the credits include Dylvinci, Wulf Morpheus, Ovrcast, Coffee Black, Jacob Rochester and AMARAH, with Amindi the one guest, on "Trip."

Thompson called it "intimate by design but expansive in scope." Mavi has tied the record to grief, including news of an uncle's death that reached him while he was opening for Jack Harlow on the Creme De La Creme tour with Babyface Ray, per Rolling Stone.

years.big: Zora Neale Hurston's trickster hero, retold as a way to survive
q: Laughter is liberation within the black body.
years.src: Passion of the Weiss · Rolling Stone
years.h: The title comes from High John the Conqueror
years.p: Mavi took the folklore from Hurston's retelling and read laughter as a way through loss, not around it.
years.xp: Mavi told Passion of the Weiss the record draws on Hurston's telling of High John de Conqueror, the folk figure who survives by laughing. He has framed the album as a person transformed by loss and kept standing by that.

years.h: Four year-end lists: Okayplayer No. 9, Pitchfork No. 34, NPR No. 36, Rolling Stone No. 47
years.p: Album of the Year tallies the placements for Laughing So Hard, It Hurts across major outlets.
years.xp: Album of the Year lists the album at No. 9 at Okayplayer, No. 34 at Pitchfork, No. 36 at NPR Music and No. 47 at Rolling Stone. Its critic score there, from two reviews, is 85: Pitchfork 82 and HipHopDX 88.

years.p: The NPR-distributed interview show talks to Mavi about the album, loss and keeping a 16-track record to just over 30 minutes.

eras.title: Shadows, then sober
eras.text: A darker record, then a brighter one on a real label, with the first guests of his career.

years.p: Pitchfork's Dash Lewis called it "among his darkest work, but also his most piercing and inventive," per Album of the Year.
years.xp: Production credits include TwoTone, Beach Noise, Angelo LeRoi and Psymun. Album of the Year lists it as a self-release.

years.h: The Pilot is out on Loma Vista, with guests
years.p: Earl Sweatshirt, Smino, MIKE and Kenny Mason appear on the mixtape, which Wikipedia calls Mavi's first project with guest features.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the mixtape documents his first year of sobriety, with production from Sango, Nephew Hesh, Angelo LeRoi, Asean Bwoy and others. Pitchfork's Stephen Kearse gave it 7.4, writing that Mavi presents "every version of himself all at once."
